schema: Milestone 17: the key terms the reader underlines. Every concept of the concept index (sources/concepts) is a term already; this file adds the Neoplatonic vocabulary the index lacks, and for any term: a one-line plain meaning (the Workshop's own words), Taylor's English forms (and the other translators'), fixed English phrases, extra Greek words, passages and later readings. Each English form and phrase carries a quotation showing it used: source 'taylor-terms' (Taylor's Explanation of Certain Platonic Terms), 'taylor-introduction' (his General Introduction, 1804), a book of the concept index (plotinus-taylor-1817, proclus-theology-taylor-1816, iamblichus-taylor-1821), 'translation' (an English translation at a Stephanus section: edition, work, ref) or 'plato' (Burnet's Greek). tools/terms.py looks for every quotation, and for the form inside it. A lemma's rule: all (every word tagged with it is underlined), with-article (only neuter with the article, as a name: τὸ ἕν), none (listed, not underlined). key false: listed, opens from the word box, not underlined.
about: The words of Plato and the Platonists that the reader underlines, so that an idea can be followed from the page being read into every dialogue and into the Platonists.

terms.label: The One
terms.plain: The first cause of all things for the later Platonists, simpler than anything and beyond being itself; Taylor says it is what the Republic calls the good and the Parmenides calls the one.

lemmas.why: εἷς is mostly the number one; only τὸ ἕν, 'the one', used as a name, is marked

english.quote: whom in the Republic he calls the good, and in the Parmenides the one, is not only above soul and intellect, but is even superior to being itself
if the one exists, the one cannot be many, can it?

phrases.quote: the united is not the one itself, but that which is passive to it

passages.why: The first hypothesis of the Parmenides: if the one is, it cannot be many.

passages.quote: τὸ ἓν μὴ τῶν γιγνομένων τε καὶ ἀπολλυμένων
passages.why: The Philebus: the unities that are not things which come to be and perish.

later.quote: the highest God, whom in the Republic he calls the good, and in the Parmenides the one
later.says: Taylor: the good of the Republic and the one of the Parmenides are the same highest God.

terms.plain: How one thing can also be many, and many one: the question of the Parmenides and the Philebus, which for the later Platonists runs through every level of things.

lemmas.why: τὸ ἕν is marked as the One

terms.plain: The highest thing in the Republic, the cause of knowledge and truth and 'beyond being'; the later Platonists take it to be the One.

english.quote: whom in the Republic he calls the good
whilst the good itself is not essence, but beyond essence

phrases.quote: separating the idea of the good from all others
elevates those that use it, to the good itself, and the first unities

terms.plain: Beauty itself, one and unchanging, which all beautiful things share in; the goal of the ascent in Diotima's speech in the Symposium.

english.quote: betaking himself to the ample sea of beauty
if this world is beautiful, and its artificer good

phrases.quote: he at length arrives at the beautiful itself

terms.plain: What is as it is said to be; for Plato the Good gives truth to what is known, as the sun gives light to what is seen.

english.quote: Truth, αληθεια. Plato, following ancient theologists. considers truth multifariously.

lemmas.why: εἰμί is mostly 'is'; only τὸ ὄν, τὰ ὄντα, 'being' and 'the things that are', used as names, are marked, and not τῷ ὄντι, which LSJ gives as 'in reality, in fact'

terms.plain: What truly is, always the same and known by intellect, as against what comes to be and passes away; Taylor renders Plato's οὐσία 'essence'.

english.quote: their being and essence are thence derived
whilst the good itself is not essence, but beyond essence
their very existence and essence is derived to them from it

phrases.quote: but is even superior to being itself

terms.plain: What comes to be and passes away and never simply is: the world of the senses; Taylor's word is 'generation'.

english.quote: Generation, γενεσις. An essence composite and multiform, and conjoined with time.
the supreme originating principle of Becoming and the Cosmos

terms.plain: The unchanging realities that things are named after and share in (beauty itself, justice itself); Plato's εἶδος and ἰδέα, which Taylor renders 'form' and 'idea'.

english.quote: but what that form itself is by which all holy things are
things unholy are unholy by one idea
in each of these ideas subsist

phrases.quote: is the self-identical Form, ungenerated and indestructible

terms.plain: The highest power of the soul, which sees the truth directly and not by reasoning; for the later Platonists also a divine order above soul and below the One.

english.quote: Intellect. (nous) In the human soul is the summit of dianoia
it is the mind that arranges and causes all things
you do not think they possess true intelligence about them

phrases.quote: that we must say it was prudent in Intellect not to contend for that prize

terms.plain: Speech, reasoned account and reason itself; for the later Platonists also the forming principles (logoi) by which soul and nature shape things.

english.quote: Reason, λογος. This word in Platonic writers signifies either that inward discursive energy called reasoning
Reasons. (logoi) Productive principles or powers
who is able to exact an account of the essence of each thing

terms.plain: What gives life and moves itself; for the Platonists the level between intellect and body, in each living thing and in the world as a whole.

english.quote: Psychical, ψυχικος. Pertaining to soul.

phrases.quote: And in the midst thereof He set Soul

terms.plain: The maker of the ordered world in the Timaeus, who, being good, made it as like himself as he could; Taylor calls him the Demiurgus, the artificer of the universe.

lemmas.why: mostly 'poet'; the maker of the Timaeus is marked by δημιουργός

english.quote: Demiurgus, δημιουργος. Jupiter, the artificer of the universe.
Demiurgus, δημιουργος. Jupiter, the artificer of the universe.
its Constructor good
also in the habit of saying that the craftsman who produces either of them fixes

phrases.quote: to discover the Maker and Father of this Universe
the father and maker of all this universe is past finding out

terms.plain: What is known by intellect and not by the senses: the Forms, and for the later Platonists the highest order of being.

english.quote: Intelligible, the, το νοητον. This word in Plato and Platonic writers has a various signification
the things themselves are intelligibles

phrases.quote: perceptible God made in the image of the Intelligible, most great and good and fair

terms.plain: What is perceived by the senses: the visible world of things that come to be and pass away, an image of the intelligible.

english.quote: surely apprehend the two types, the visible and the intelligible. I do. Represent
all sensible things are apprehended by opinion and sense

terms.plain: How a thing has a character by sharing in the Form of it: beautiful things are beautiful by sharing in beauty itself.

english.quote: all the multitude of beautiful things partake of it
for thus it would be being, and participate of essence
they possess the good according to participation

terms.plain: The going out of all things from the One, each level from the one above it, while the cause stays as it was; Taylor's word is 'progression'. Plato has no word for it.

english.quote: imitating the progression of beings from the one, and their conversion to it again
while it proceeds from, at the same time abides in, and returns to its leader

terms.plain: The turning back of each thing to the cause it came from, which completes procession; in Plato, the turning of the whole soul round toward the light (Republic VII).

english.quote: would appear to be the art of his conversion
imitating the progression of beings from the one, and their conversion to it again

terms.plain: Firm understanding of what always is, which can give the reason why; Taylor's word for ἐπιστήμη is 'science'.

english.quote: Science. This word is sometimes defined by Plato to be that which assigns the causes of things
the objects of knowledge

terms.plain: Belief about what can be otherwise: it can be true or false, and knows that a thing is but not why.

english.quote: Opinion. (doxa) Is the last of the gnostic powers of the rational soul

terms.plain: Thinking that reasons step by step from starting-points, as geometry does: in the divided line, the level below intellect.

english.quote: Dianoia, διανοια, from whence dianoetic, the discursive energy of reason
Dianoia, διανοια, from whence dianoetic, the discursive energy of reason
you regard understanding as something intermediate between opinion and reason

terms.plain: The excellence of a thing, and of a soul above all; for the later Platonists a ladder of virtues by which the soul rises.

english.quote: the other so-called virtues of the soul

terms.plain: In the Republic, each part of the soul, and each class in the city, doing its own work.

english.quote: and ordered him to bring Shame and Justice to men, that these two might be
the just man must wish to do what is

terms.plain: The Platonists' view that evil is not a thing in its own right but a lack or falling short of good.
The relation of a copy to its model: the world is an image made after an eternal pattern, as reflections are images of things.

english.quote: Paradigm, παραδειγμα. A pattern, or that with reference to which a thing is made.
Paradigm, παραδειγμα. A pattern, or that with reference to which a thing is made.
a certain movable image of eternity
he looked towards an eternal exemplar in its fabrication

terms.plain: The soul's rise from the things of sense to what truly is, as from the cave to the sun, or up Diotima's ladder of beauty.
The teaching that learning is remembering what the soul knew before birth.

english.quote: our learning is nothing else than recollection
learning, with respect to us, is nothing else than reminiscence

terms.plain: What is without time altogether, whole at once; Taylor distinguishes it from the perpetual, which lasts through all time.

english.quote: Eternal, the, το αιωνιον, that which has a never-ending subsistence, without any connection with time
a certain movable image of eternity
Perpetual, the, το αιδιον. That which subsists forever, but through a connection with time.

phrases.quote: he fixed his gaze on the Eternal

terms.plain: The gods, and the god of the dialogues; for the later Platonists a whole order of gods proceeding from the One.
What belongs to the gods; Taylor: being joined to the One, as essence, life and intellect are when they are made divine.

english.quote: Divine, the, το ϑειον, is being subsisting in conjunction with the one.

terms.plain: Taylor's word for the very first ground of a thing's being, 'the summit of essence'.

english.quote: Hyparxis, υπαρξις. The first principle or foundation, as it were, of the essence of a thing.

terms.plain: A unit that holds a many within itself and gives rise to it: the head of each order of things.

english.quote: Monad, μονας, in divine natures is that which contains distinct, but at the same time profoundly-united multitude
whether such monads should be deemed to have true being

terms.plain: A cause that stays above what shares in it and is not mixed into it, as imparticipable intellect is above every particular intellect.

terms.label: Henads (unities)
terms.plain: A unity: the Philebus asks about such unities (man, ox, beauty, the good); for Proclus the gods themselves are the unities that come first after the One.

english.quote: the intense interest in these and similar unities
whether such monads should be deemed to have true being
elevates those that use it, to the good itself, and the first unities

passages.why: Socrates on the unities that are not things which come to be and perish: man, ox, the beautiful, the good.

terms.label: Bound and the infinite
terms.plain: The two principles of the Philebus from which all mixed things come; for the later Platonists the first pair after the One, from which being is mixed.

english.quote: have in themselves bound and infinity connatural
have in themselves bound and infinity connatural
have inherent in them the finite and the infinite
have inherent in them the finite and the infinite

phrases.quote: the two first principles of things (bound and infinity)

passages.quote: πέρας δὲ καὶ ἀπειρίαν ἐν αὑτοῖς σύμφυτον ἐχόντων
passages.why: The gift of the gods: all things are from one and many, and have limit and the unlimited in them.

passages.quote: τὸ μὲν ἄπειρον δεῖξαι τῶν ὄντων, τὸ δὲ πέρας
passages.why: The four kinds of the Philebus begin with the unlimited and the limit.

later.quote: If also being is composed from the elements bound and infinity, as appears from the Philebus of Plato
later.says: Taylor: being is composed of bound and infinity, as the Philebus shows.

terms.label: Life
terms.plain: Life itself: for the later Platonists the middle of the triad being, life and intellect; the Sophist asks whether what perfectly is can be without life and soul and intellect.

english.quote: motion and life and soul and mind are really not present to absolute being

passages.quote: κίνησιν καὶ ζωὴν καὶ ψυχὴν καὶ φρόνησιν
passages.why: The Eleatic Stranger: can we believe that motion, life, soul and wisdom are not present to what perfectly is?

later.quote: we next see being, life, intellect, soul, nature and body depending
later.says: Taylor: below the One come being, life, intellect, soul, nature and body.

terms.label: Nature
terms.plain: What a thing is by birth and growth, and the whole order of such things; for the later Platonists the level below soul that shapes bodies.

english.quote: say that nature is defective and lame

later.quote: we next see being, life, intellect, soul, nature and body depending
later.says: Taylor: nature comes after soul and before body.

terms.plain: The receptacle of the Timaeus, in which the images of the Forms come to be, 'the nurse of becoming'; later called matter.

english.quote: of being? We reply, that it is the receptacle, and in a manner the nurse, of
liken the Recipient to the Mother

terms.plain: The soul of the whole world, which the maker of the Timaeus set in its midst and stretched through it all.
Spirits between gods and men, as Love is in the Symposium, carrying prayers up and gifts down.

english.quote: A great daemon replied
And what is that, Diotima? A great spirit, Socrates: for the whole of the

terms.plain: Love as the longing for what one lacks, the beautiful and the good, which can lead the soul upward.

english.quote: their honor by the poets, the god of Love, so ancient and so great

terms.plain: The highest way of thinking in the Republic: reasoning by question and answer up to the first principle, without the senses.

english.quote: skilled in dialectic
by the power of dialectics

terms.plain: The goal of life for the Platonists after the Theaetetus: to become as like god as a human can, by becoming just and wise.
The soul's not dying: argued in the Phaedo, and in the Phaedrus from the soul's moving itself.

english.quote: Every soul is immortal

terms.plain: Practical wisdom, seeing what is good to do; Taylor's word is 'prudence'.

english.quote: Prudence, φρονιησις. This word frequently means in Plato and Platonic writers
are to be bought and sold, is in fact wisdom; and courage and self-restraint

terms.plain: That because of which a thing is; Taylor lists the Platonists' six kinds of cause (the end, the pattern, the maker, the instrument, the form, the matter).

english.quote: the mind should be the cause of all things

terms.plain: The Republic's image of a line cut into four: images, visible things, the objects of reasoning and the Forms, with the four states of mind that grasp them.
What is not: the Sophist shows that it is, in a way, as 'the other' than what is.
A triad the Greek scholia name in the divine: will, power and intellect.
Taylor's word for ξένος, the visitor or stranger of the Sophist, Statesman and Laws: one who receives or is received as a guest.
